title: ABEAR Code of Conduct Violations — LATAM Brazil's Systematic Breach of Industry Self‑Regulation Standards on Ethics, Transparency, and Consumer Protection
incident_timestamp_display: 4 April 2024 (GRU) and 5 July 2024 (SCL) — ABEAR violations span both incidents
allegation_summary: LATAM Airlines Brazil, a member of ABEAR (Associação Brasileira das Empresas Aéreas), systematically violated ABEAR’s Code of Conduct, which requires the highest standards of ethics, transparency, and integrity. Specific violations include: (1) Ethics — employee André BD Marinho committed criminal injúria and ameaça against a consumer (I‑001); (2) Transparency — LATAM maintained false accusations of aggression despite PDI exoneration, withheld CCTV evidence, and refused to provide written documentation of the lifetime ban (I‑002); (3) Integrity — LATAM engaged in KPI manipulation, case fragmentation, and gaslighting communications (both incidents). The former ANAC President, Juliano Noman, now serves as ABEAR President, creating a structural conflict where the industry self‑regulation body is led by the former head of the regulator that improperly dismissed the complaint. This situation exacerbates the code of conduct violations by undermining ABEAR’s capacity to objectively enforce its standards against LATAM.
